_doc: 09-map-land-starter-city.md §2.11 / §8.2. Created by doc 92 §19 (audit 91 D-7) — report 98 G-1 named this file and moved doc 02's ladder into it, but nothing ever wrote it, so `sim/population/progression_system.gd` carried the six rows as a `const` and the ladder was the one balance number in the game with no data file. It has one now. Doc 09 §8.2 also authors `population`, `happiness`, `milestones`, `stats_counters` and `bench_city` blocks for this file; those consumers still hold their own constants and moving them is not doc 92 §19's pass. Do not add a second copy of anything here — this is the ladder's only home, and ProgressionSystem's `CITY_LEVEL_POP_FALLBACK` is a missing-file degrade, not a mirror.
_thresholds_note: RETUNED by doc 92 §19 against §19.1's measured population curves: [0, 250, 1000, 4000, 12000, 30000] -> the rows below. The old ladder was adopted verbatim from a doc 02 proposal that predated any measurement, and the measurement is damning: over 90 game-days the fastest builder in the study peaks at 1,872 residents (doc 92 §8) and the competent player ends FIFTY game-days at 2,710 (§19.1), so four of the six rungs were unreachable by anything the game can do and the city sat at level 2 forever. Audit 91 D-7 is the player-facing face of that: a 12-game-day city at level 0 refusing 376 upgrades with E_CITY_LEVEL. The rungs are now PLACED ON THE MEASURED CURVE of `balanced` — doc 92 §2's 'competent but not optimal' player — on a cadence that roughly doubles the game-days between rungs: level 1 on game-day 2, level 2 on game-day 11, level 3 on game-day 27. Levels 4 and 5 are outside the fifty-game-day measured window and are placed by the 2.25x ratio the fitted rungs settle into, not by fit; doc 92 §19.2 says so and names what would move them. Monotone (§2.11) is unchanged: retuning a threshold DOWN can only grant a level, never take one back.
